scan_scope.method: mmap + bytes.find(RTTI_PREFIX) descriptor walk; numpy section histograms; no IDA, no execution of either binary

fm.verdict: NOT packed / NOT encrypted at the section level: 7,538 unique plaintext MSVC RTTI type-descriptor strings are recoverable, 7,538 of them with an intact MSVC TypeDescriptor header (zeroed spare field). No high-entropy code/data section is required to explain the RTTI set.

editor.verdict: NOT packed / NOT encrypted at the section level: 1,854 unique plaintext MSVC RTTI type-descriptor strings are recoverable, 1,854 of them with an intact MSVC TypeDescriptor header (zeroed spare field). No high-entropy code/data section is required to explain the RTTI set.

database_namespace.label: `db` namespace == the brief's `DATABASE::` table population (MSVC emits `.?AV<CLASS>@db@@`), plus any `db::<sub>` families

database_named_classes.label: descriptors whose CLASS NAME contains the literal token DATABASE

brief_regex_union.label: exact population matched by the brief's regex (db:: + DATABASE:: families)

measured_directly: PE headers, sections, characteristics, entropy/histograms (full section bytes)
every b'.?AV' occurrence + descriptor string + section + TypeDescriptor header check
every occurrence of each archive filename / magic needle, with section + context
4CC literal counts (dictionary) and 4CC-shaped imm32 literal counts (structural)
not_claimed: no claim about runtime behaviour or loader code paths of fm.exe
no claim that a 4CC literal implies a live serializer - only a byte-level coincidence of an immediate operand with a known DB property code
0x0DF1 hits are counted as raw byte patterns (no instruction-level operand proof)
absence of a string in a binary is only a statement about these exact bytes
